questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I have been to Paris last year.
I have went to Paris last year.
I have gone to Paris last year.
I had went to Paris last year.
questions.answer: I have been to Paris last year.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: If it rains, I stay at home.
If it rains, I stayed at home.
If it rains, I will stay at home.
If it rains, I would stay at home.
questions.answer: If it rains, I will stay at home.

questions.question: Select the right form.
options: She has lived in London since 2010, so she knows the city well.
She has lived in London since 2010, so she knows the city good.
She has lived in London since 2010, so she knows the city very well.
She has lived in London since 2010, so she knows the city much.
questions.answer: She has lived in London since 2010, so she knows the city well.

questions.question: Which option is grammatically correct?
options: I am happy to see you yesterday.
I was happy to see you yesterday.
I am happy to see you yesterday.
I was happy to see you yesterday.
questions.answer: I was happy to see you yesterday.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I am going to study English next week.
I am going to study English next week.
I am going to study English next week.
I am going to study English next week.
questions.answer: I am going to study English next week.

questions.question: Select the right comparative form.

This book is more interesting than that one.
questions.answer: This book is more interesting than that one.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: If I had more time, I would learn Spanish.

If I had more time, I would learn Spanish.
If I had more time, I would learn Spanish.
questions.answer: If I had more time, I would learn Spanish.

questions.question: Choose the correct modal verb.
options: You should finish your homework before going out.
You should finish your homework before going out.
You should finish your homework before going out.
You should finish your homework before going out.
questions.answer: You should finish your homework before going out.

questions.question: Select the correct form of the verb.
options: Having finished my work, I went home.
Having finished my work, I went home.
Having finished my work, I went home.
Having finished my work, I went home.
questions.answer: Having finished my work, I went home.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: I like swimming in the sea, but I prefer surfing in the waves.
I like swimming in the sea, but I prefer surfing in the waves.
I like swimming in the sea, but I prefer surfing in the waves.
I like swimming in the sea, but I prefer surfing in the waves.
questions.answer: I like swimming in the sea, but I prefer surfing in the waves.
